cf.title: Fix initial sync of zero-column published tables

input.subject: [PATCH v1] Fix initial sync of zero-column published tables

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The thread states the bug with a reproducer, and Peter Smith reproduced it and confirmed the fix in message #3. The fix adds one C entry point used only by tablesync and leaves BeginCopyFrom() unchanged. Confidence is medium because the code was not read and the backpatch range is still open.

brief.title: Fix initial sync of zero-column published tables
brief.problem: When a published table has zero columns and the subscriber table has extra columns, initial table synchronization mishandles those columns. In text mode COPY stores an empty string instead of the subscriber default, while later incremental inserts use the default. In binary mode the initial copy fails with "row field count is 0, expected 1".
brief.proposed_design: Tablesync passes an empty column list, which BeginCopyFrom() reads as "all columns". The patch adds BeginCopyFromExtended() with a flag that marks the column list as explicit, and tablesync uses it so an empty list stays empty. BeginCopyFrom() keeps its behavior for SQL COPY, file_fdw and other callers.
user_visible_surface: C API: new function BeginCopyFromExtended() in commands/copy.h, with a flag for an explicit column list.
Behavior: initial sync of a zero-column published table now fills subscriber-only columns with their defaults, in text and binary modes.
author_claims: There are no SQL syntax or replication protocol changes, and the patch does not change which publisher columns are replicated.
New tests in 008_diff_schema.pl fail without the fix and pass with it, in text and binary modes.
Related subscription, COPY and file_fdw tests pass, and the patch was tested on master only.
The text-mode bug reproduces on PG10, and the binary case likely affects PG16 and later.
The patch should be backpatched to all affected supported branches.
brief.thread_state: Peter Smith reproduced the bug, confirmed the fix, and gave comment and test-style feedback, and vignesh C asked for test changes and the backpatch range. The author posted v3 with all suggestions applied; the backpatch decision is still open and no committer has replied.
unclear: The proposal does not say how a new exported function in copy.h will be handled on back branches, where the ABI must stay stable.
The patch was not tested on any back branch, and the bug was reproduced only on PG10 and master.
The proposal does not say whether other callers of BeginCopyFrom() can pass an empty list with the same mistaken meaning.

touch_points.reason: The patch changes tablesync.c, so initial sync of a logical replication subscriber behaves differently for zero-column published tables.

touch_points.reason: The patch adds the exported function BeginCopyFromExtended() to commands/copy.h.

touch_points.reason: The author asks for a backpatch to all affected branches, but tested master only and the range is not settled.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: COPY FROM gets a second entry point, BeginCopyFromExtended(), that future changes to BeginCopyFrom() must keep in step.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Which supported branches show the text-mode bug and which show the binary-mode failure, and does the patch apply and pass its tests on each of them?
Should the back branches get the new exported function BeginCopyFromExtended(), or a fix that stays inside tablesync.c, with the API change on master only?
Can any other caller of BeginCopyFrom() pass an empty column list and mean "no columns" instead of "all columns"?
What should users do with rows that an earlier initial sync already stored with an empty string, and will the release note say so?

committability.owner_note: A committer who knows logical replication tablesync and the COPY FROM code would have to own it; none has replied in the visible thread.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a new exported COPY entry point on every branch that gets the fix, and for a behavior change in initial sync on stable branches.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted a reproducer in message #2 and, per the thread state, a v3 that applies all review suggestions within about a week.

priority.reason: The bug needs a zero-column published table and extra subscriber columns, which is rare, but it stores wrong data in text mode and fails in binary mode. The patch is 7.5 KB in four files and reviewed by two people; it waits for a committer and a backpatch decision.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the review could not check that the explicit-list flag reaches every place where COPY FROM resolves the column list and prepares defaults. Behavior on back branches is untested.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Warning for Datatype mismatch between subscriber table and publisher table for logical replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes logical replication emit a warning when a subscriber table column has a different data type from the matching publisher column. The goal is to show type mismatches early so users can debug replication problems.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author did not revise the patch after review, and it had not passed CI since about mid March, so the CF entry was closed. Ashutosh Bapat had asked for the unrelated file renames to be removed. He also noted that the code maps columns by position, and that it compares type OIDs and names on the subscriber without using the remote type cache.

precedents_retrieved.title: Multi-column list partitioning
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds multi-column list partitioning, so that `partition by list (a, b)` takes partitions defined by value tuples such as `for values in (1, 2), (1, 5)`. It changes bound transformation, the bound data structures, tuple routing, partition pruning, NULL handling and, in a split second patch, partition-wise join.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Amul Sul questioned the pruning design. Range partitioning needs a prefix of the partition keys, but list partitions could also be pruned on later keys alone, and he judged the NULL handling in pruning to be wrong. Julien Rouhaud set the entry to Waiting on Author because of these concerns and a clang warning. The visible messages show no new patch or author reply before the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I haven't studied the whole partition pruning code and don't know the complete code flow, but AFAICU, this is not the correct way to handle null value.

precedents_retrieved.title: [PROPOSAL] : Disallow use of empty column name in (column_name '') in ALTER or CREATE of foreign table.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes postgres_fdw's validator reject empty values for the column_name, schema_name and table_name options in create or alter foreign table. Today an empty column_name is accepted, and the remote query then fails with a zero-length identifier error.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane judged that the check did not add enough ease-of-use to justify the extra code, and he compared an empty name to a misspelled remote name, which cannot be checked either. Robert Haas pointed out that existing foreign tables with empty values would then fail pg_dump or pg_upgrade. Nobody argued for the patch after Tom voted against it, so Robert marked it Rejected.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I was down on it to start with, on the grounds that it wasn't adding enough ease-of-use to justify even a relatively small amount of added code.

precedents_retrieved.title: Time-delayed logical replication subscriber
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Masahiko Sawada, Nathan Bossart, Amit Kapila
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a subscription option that delays applying logical replication changes by a set time, like recovery_min_apply_delay for standbys. Later versions moved the wait to the publisher as min_send_delay, with the walsender holding back each transaction and the combination with streaming = parallel disallowed.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The subscriber confirms the flush LSN only after it commits the delayed transaction, so the publisher cannot advance restart_lsn or xmin during the delay. With delays of hours or days, WAL builds up on the publisher and VACUUM cannot remove dead rows, and users have no setting to avoid this. Reviewers asked for a different design, such as having the subscriber write decoded changes to disk first or adding a walreceiver process, and the author closed the entry to work on that.

precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
IMO the current set of
trade-offs (e.g., unavoidable bloat and WAL buildup) would make this
feature virtually unusable for a lot of workloads, so it's probably worth
exploring an alternative approach.

precedents_retrieved.title: tablesync early exit
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes a tablesync worker call process_syncing_tables() before it enters the apply main loop, so a worker with nothing left to do exits early. The author presented it as a small optimization and as a cleaner split of work between tablesync and apply workers.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Amit Kapila objected that exiting before the tablesync worker receives any message skips changes up to the LSN where the copy finished. That is safe with the current code but would lose changes for the table in a design where the apply worker applies streamed in-progress transactions, which had already been proposed on -hackers. The saving was only the work to receive messages for one transaction, so the author withdrew the patch.
matched_queries: binary copy field count mismatch tablesync
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
As per my understanding, this is safe as per the current code but it
can't be guaranteed for future implementations and the amount of extra
work is additional work to receive the messages for one transaction.

precedents_retrieved.title: Table AM modifications to accept column projection lists
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes the table AM API so that sequential scans, index scans, tuple_lock and tuple fetch take a column projection set, so that columnar AMs such as Zedstore read only the columns a query needs. The planner and executor collect these sets, for example scanCols and returningCols in RangeTblEntry, with separate sets for RETURNING, EPQ checks and ON CONFLICT UPDATE.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The authors withdrew the patch. They said it was hard to review in its current form and that no concrete implementation of the new API existed in core, and they had no time to improve it before the July commitfest. Reviewers had raised smaller points, such as adding scan_begin_with_column_projection as a new callback instead of extending scan_begin, but nobody objected to the design.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
We agree that
it's fairly difficult to review in its current state, and the lack of a
concrete implementation of the new API isn't helping.

precedents_retrieved.title: speed up a logical replication setup (pg_subscriber)
precedents_retrieved.summary: A new client tool, pg_subscriber, converts a physical standby or a restored base backup into a logical replica. It creates replication slots and publications on the source, recovers the target to a consistent LSN, then creates and enables subscriptions starting from that LSN.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry was returned with feedback because it waited on author input for about two weeks or more, and no new patch version appears in the visible messages. Open review points included changing the system identifier of the converted server (Andres Freund), the tool name, an option to run pg_basebackup, needed test cases, and code structure and refactoring issues raised by Peter Eisentraut.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the corpus search returned no earlier proposal with the same or a similar idea, and no thread message points to an earlier discussion. From the prior-attempts angle there is no recorded rejection reason to apply to this bug fix.

From the standards and compatibility angle there is no objection. The patch adds no SQL syntax, GUC, catalog state, dump output or protocol change. It fixes a subscriber-only divergence: initial sync stored '' where later inserts used the subscriber default. Adding BeginCopyFromExtended() beside an unchanged BeginCopyFrom() follows the existing *Extended naming pattern, and on back branches it adds a symbol without changing an existing signature. A committer would likely confirm two points. First, the fix runs on the subscriber, so the publisher version does not matter. Second, rows already synced with '' stay as they are after a minor upgrade, and the release note could say so.

The fix changes only how the subscriber reads an empty column list, so no WAL, protocol, catalog or on-disk change follows, and mixed publisher versions behave the same. On back branches the patch adds BeginCopyFromExtended() and leaves BeginCopyFrom() unchanged, which keeps the ABI; rows already synced with '' stay as they are and need a release note.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. With the fix, tablesync evaluates subscriber default expressions for subscriber-only columns, which the apply worker already does for incremental inserts under the same role, so no new code runs and no new data or privilege becomes reachable. The new BeginCopyFromExtended() is a C entry point and adds nothing callable from SQL.

This is a narrow bug fix with a reproducer, confirmed in message #3, and it adds nothing to the hot path. A committer may still ask whether master should take a different API shape than the back branches, but no concrete failure scenario follows from adding BeginCopyFromExtended(). Committability: no committer has replied, although the author keeps answering review.

This is a bug fix for tablesync. No existing feature, option or extension lets tablesync pass an explicitly empty column list to COPY, so the need is not met elsewhere. An *Extended() variant of an existing function follows common Postgres practice. The back-branch ABI and backpatch-range questions fall under other angles.

This is a bug fix, so demand is not the test: initial sync stores '' where incremental apply stores the default, and binary sync fails outright. Peter Smith reproduced it independently (message #3). The cost is one internal COPY entry point used only by tablesync.
